title: Principles of Quantum Superposition
text:
Superposition is a fundamental concept in quantum mechanics describing the ability of a quantum system to exist in multiple states simultaneously. Before measurement, a particle such as an electron does not possess a single defined location or spin; rather, it exists as a weighted combination of all possible states.

The act of observation collapses this superposition into a single definite state, which is analogous to solving a wave function. This probabilistic nature dictates that the outcomes are governed by mathematical probability amplitudes rather than classical certainties.

Understanding superposition challenges classical intuition regarding objective reality and provides the foundation for quantum computing's ability to process exponentially more information.
